claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a hierarchical heterostructure containing intragranular nanoprecipitates.
Nanoprecipitate size, distribution, and grain-boundary character can be acquired at high resolution during mechanical testing.
The hierarchical distribution of nanoprecipitates modulates local dislocation motion in HfNbTiVAl10.
Grain-boundary and compositional variations modulate local stress distributions in HfNbTiVAl10.
Microstructural heterogeneity controls activation of dislocation-based deformation in HfNbTiVAl10.
Microstructural heterogeneity controls crack initiation mechanisms in HfNbTiVAl10.
Real-time microstructural descriptors will enable a machine-learning model to reproduce the alloy's mechanical response more accurately than established simulations.
The descriptor-integrated model will predict Young's modulus more accurately than established simulations.
The descriptor-integrated model will predict yield strength more accurately than established simulations.
The descriptor-integrated model will predict fracture-related behavior more accurately than established simulations.
Prediction error for Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness will be reduced by roughly 20% relative to established simulations.
Prediction time will be reduced by around 50% relative to established simulations.
Established finite-element and constitutive simulations used as the baseline do not incorporate live microstructural descriptors.
The model may fail when high-temperature creep or rate-dependent deformation mechanisms dominate.
The model may fail when imaging limitations prevent reliable quantification of the microstructural descriptors.
The proposed comparison is limited to room-temperature tests without aggressive environmental exposure.
Failure to obtain both at least a 20% error reduction and a 50% time reduction under identical conditions will falsify the hypothesis.
